chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Hamzah ibn Humran, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I enter the market and wish to buy a female slave, and she says, 'I am free (manumulated).'' He said, 'Buy her, unless she has proof.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying a slave who claims to be free?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the default legal presumption (*asl*) of continued slavery for a female slave claiming freedom, requiring her to provide conclusive proof (*bayyinah*) to overturn it. This ruling reflects the classical Shia juristic approach to manumission, emphasizing that the burden of proof lies with the claimant to demonstrate a valid deed of freedom or prior agreement. It serves as a foundational text for understanding property rights and evidentiary standards in Islamic commercial law.
